hypothesis: Peeled software-pipelined K-loop with prologue tl.load A/B and per-trip tl.load next-A/next-B before tl.dot current will outperform baseline by overlapping global loads with MMA while keeping single tl.dot per tile.
expected_mechanism: Prologue issues tl.load a_cur/b_cur with hoisted m_mask/n_mask, each loop trip issues tl.load a_nxt from a_ptrs+BK and b_nxt from b_ptrs+BK*N with k_next+BK masks before tl.dot a_cur,b_cur into FP32 acc, then rotates cur=nxt and does single a_ptrs+=BK and b_ptrs+=BK*N advances plus trailing tl.dot, so the num_stages=3 pipeliner can overlap next-tile global loads with current-tile dot while reusing m_mask/n_mask in tl.load and tl.store masks.
reasoning_from_feedback: This differs from the prior unevaluated review which is two-slab unrolling with two tl.load A/B and two tl.dot per trip and 2*BK pointer advances and is still not compiled/checked/timed, so no measured feedback is claimed for it. It differs from trusted-two-slab k_loop_unrolling which had screening loss and doubled shared memory/mma sites with 12 trips x 2 dots; this keeps single tl.dot per logical tile, single BK advances, and rotates one live buffer to avoid extra staging. It reuses the trusted-compute mask_hoisting idea of hoisted m_mask/n_mask but the main change is load-next-before-dot-current reordering with prologue/epilog rather than only mask arithmetic and tl.range hint. It keeps baseline program-ID mapping and avoids reviewed structural Split-K global reduction and Grouped-M4 swizzle. Each screening ratio belongs to its paired run with timing_directly_comparable false, so absolute times are not pooled and a trusted result belongs only to its independently written implementation.
